title: Siadenovirus Coverage Audit
standfirst: Siadenoviruses carry the smallest adenovirus genomes, about 26 kb, and the core gene set with very few extras. The module calls every core gene in every genome that has sequence to call; the 10 poor genomes are deposits with no cytosine at all.
headline_tiles: fewer distinct strings at equal depth

sections.title: What the module covers
sections.lede: Siadenoviruses of birds, reptiles and amphibians (turkey adenovirus 3, frog adenovirus 1, penguin and raptor siadenoviruses).

blocks.html: Turkey adenovirus 3 carries the siadenovirus core and its few genus genes (sialidase, E3, hydrophobic protein, ORF7, ORF8).

Genomes were assigned to modules from sequence alone: the genus by best hexon match, and one-fiber versus multi-fiber mastadenoviruses by a census of intact fiber genes classed by literature orthology (Podgorski 2023, PMID 36610683). Deposited names were never used to assign a genome.

sections.title: How it was built
sections.lede: Membership by homology to curated seed collections; the deposited name is recorded but never decides.

rows: 415 unique proteins assigned (≥80% coverage both ways, best feature ≥1.2× the runner-up)
73 no hit, 0 ambiguous, 13 low coverage, 0 submitter-marked partial

blocks.html: Paralogue families were split into orthogroup features by genome position, and each is called by sequence, never by location. Features with no literature function are named “Uncharacterized lineage-specific protein”. Splice junctions come from the literature and were extended to other lineages by aligning donor and acceptor sites; every spliced product was translated and checked in frame.
Self-recall (each feature’s profiles searched against its own collection) is 100% for nearly every feature; the registry page lists every feature.

sections.title: Where the cutoffs sit
sections.lede: Cutoffs left at the default are not listed; every one below was set from a measurement.

blocks.html: No feature needed a cutoff away from the default.

Every CDS scans to its stop codon (downstream_ext 1); mature peptides set both extension flags from their own termini. In the 916-genome check, every unspliced CDS call ends on a stop codon except calls that stop at an N gap or an IUPAC base in the assembly.

sections.title: Does it route?
sections.lede: A genome no rep contig claims is never annotated at all.

blocks.html: All genomes assigned to this module route to it.

sections.title: What the run found
sections.lede: Genome quality from the GTO pipeline on the 916-genome subset, with the essential genes set by the curator’s rules.

rows: contig has too many ambiguous bases

blocks.html: Essential genes (copy_num) follow the curator’s rules: never on uncharacterized proteins, special features or lineage-specific genes, and excluded wherever a cutoff, copy-number or coverage problem is on record. Essential here: FIBER, HEXON, IVA2, K100, K22, K52, PENTON, PIIIA, POL, PROTEASE, PTP, PVI, PVII, PVIII, UXP, VII_MAT, VI_MAT.

The subset deliberately over-samples unusual genomes, so its quality rate is a floor for the module, not an estimate of it. Poor genomes are dominated by sequence problems: deposits with no cytosine, N gaps, partial genomes and genes interrupted by stop codons.

blocks.html: Unbound deposits are mostly “hypothetical protein” and deposits whose sequence was ambiguous between two features; several name proteins the module does call (for example 22K and E4 ORF1 in the one-fiber mastadenoviruses), so the unbound count is not a count of missed proteins.
